sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》的《访谈》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia Navarro.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚·纳瓦罗。

sentences.en: Are you happy?
sentences.zh: 你快乐吗？

sentences.en: It's a deceptively simple question, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个看似简单的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: But for me at least, it's a really difficult one to answer.
sentences.zh: 但至少对我来说，这真的很难回答。

sentences.en: Another tough question, why is it so hard to be happy for so many people?
sentences.zh: 另一个棘手的问题是，为什么对这么多人来说，感到快乐如此困难？

sentences.en: Despite a culture of wellness influencers with their happiness hacks and mindset tricks, all of the indicators show that we Americans are less happy than ever.
sentences.zh: 尽管现在流行着各种健康网红，推崇他们的快乐秘诀和思维技巧，但所有指标都显示，我们美国人比以往任何时候都更不快乐。

sentences.en: What is going on and what can we do about it?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？我们又能为此做些什么？

sentences.en: I put those questions to Dr. Laurie Santos.
sentences.zh: 我把这些问题抛给了劳里·桑托斯博士。

sentences.en: Santos is a cognitive scientist whose class on happiness quickly became the most popular in Yale's history.
sentences.zh: 桑托斯是一位认知科学家，她在耶鲁大学开设的关于快乐的课程迅速成为该校历史上最受欢迎的课程。

sentences.en: And through her podcast, The Happiness Lab, and her free online course called The Science of Wellbeing,
sentences.zh: 通过她的播客《快乐实验室》以及名为《幸福科学》的免费在线课程，

sentences.en: Santos' reach has extended well beyond the classroom.
sentences.zh: 桑托斯的影响力早已超出了课堂。

sentences.en: I wanted to understand what the science says happiness really is, how our understanding of what it takes to be happy has changed over time,
sentences.zh: 我想了解科学所说的“快乐”究竟是什么，我们对快乐所需的理解是如何随时间改变的，

sentences.en: and why, with the pandemic in our rearview mirror, it's still been so hard for me, and many others, to do the things that will actually make us happier.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么在疫情已成往事的情况下，我和许多人依然难以做到那些真正能让我们更快乐的事情。

sentences.en: And what you told me was surprising.
sentences.zh: 而你告诉我的答案令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Dr. Lori Santos.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与劳里·桑托斯博士的对话。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being here.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you could join me.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我参加节目。

sentences.en: I am going to start in a bit of a strange place because like so many people in the world,
sentences.zh: 我要从一个有点奇怪的地方开始，因为像世界上许多人一样，

sentences.en: I was really obsessed with the story of Punch the Monkey, that little monkey in Japan whose mother sort of rejected him and he had no one to socialize with, so he adopted that
sentences.zh: 我真的很痴迷于“Punch猴子”的故事，那只在日本的小猴子，它的母亲似乎抛弃了它，它没有同伴可以社交，所以它收养了那个

sentences.en: Ikea monkey toy.
sentences.zh: 宜家猴子玩具。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I have a theory about Punch that connects to happiness, and I wanted to put it to you because apart from being a happiness expert, you also study animal cognition
sentences.zh: 我关于Punch有一个理论，它与快乐有关，我想把它提出来，因为除了作为快乐专家，你还研究动物认知，

sentences.en: and you started your work with monkeys.
sentences.zh: 而且你的研究工作是从猴子开始的。

sentences.en: Literally everyone that I know sent me information about Punch.
sentences.zh: 我认识的每一个人都给我发了关于Punch的信息。

sentences.en: I was like getting in real time what was happening with Punch.
sentences.zh: 我当时就像在实时接收关于Punch发生的一切。

sentences.en: I was really thinking about why so many people around the world connected with Punch's inability to form relationships.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考，为什么世界各地有这么多人会对Punch无法建立关系产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And you've long said that the bonds with other people are one of the building blocks of happiness.
sentences.zh: 你一直说，与他人的纽带是快乐的基石之一。

sentences.en: It's one of the most important things that we can do.
sentences.zh: 这是我们能做的最重要的事情之一。

sentences.en: But especially here in the US, those bonds were fraying.
sentences.zh: 但特别是在美国，这些纽带正在瓦解。

sentences.en: And I think we just saw some of ourselves in punch.
sentences.zh: 我想我们只是在Punch身上看到了自己的一部分。

sentences.en: Do you think I may be right?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我说的对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it was fascinating to see just how much emotion people showed about punch, which I think is funny because sometimes we see news stories about the pain of
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看到人们对Punch表现出如此多的情感，这很迷人，我觉得这很有趣，因为有时我们看到关于

sentences.en: other actual humans and we don't show that much compassion, right?
sentences.zh: 其他真实人类痛苦的新闻报道时，却并没有表现出那么多的同情心，对吧？

sentences.en: But I think talking about the loneliness crisis through a monkey, like through this poor little monkey that didn't do anything, it wasn't really his fault.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，通过一只猴子来谈论孤独危机，通过这只什么都没做、错并不在它自己的可怜小猴子，

sentences.en: I think that really allowed us a way to talk about the loneliness crisis and to feel it and admit it in ourselves in a way that wasn't as shameful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实让我们找到了一种谈论孤独危机的方式，让我们能够感受它，并以一种不那么羞耻的方式承认它存在于我们自身。

sentences.en: You know, I spent a lot of time in advance of this conversation really thinking about the nature of happiness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这次对话之前，我花了很多时间深入思考快乐的本质。

sentences.en: And I want to start by digging into just what happiness is and maybe do some basic defining of terms because I went down a few rabbit holes.
sentences.zh: 我想从探讨快乐究竟是什么开始，也许先对术语做一些基本的定义，因为我钻进了几个牛角尖。

sentences.en: You can.
sentences.zh: 你可以的。

sentences.en: It's very easy to do with this term in particular.
sentences.zh: 对于这个词，尤其是这个词，这非常容易做到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so as I discovered, lots of philosophers have tackled the question of happiness going back to ancient Greece.
sentences.zh: 正如我所发现的，许多哲学家从古希腊开始就一直在探讨快乐的问题。

sentences.en: And there's two main types of happiness, according to ancient Greek philosophers, as far as I could tell.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，古希腊哲学家认为快乐主要有两种类型。

sentences.en: And one is hedonic and the other one is eudaimonic.
sentences.zh: 一种是享乐主义的快乐，另一种是幸福主义的快乐。

sentences.en: Can you explain what that is, what the difference is, what they were looking at back then?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下那是什么吗？区别在哪里？他们当时在研究什么？

sentences.en: So hedonic happiness, I think, is what a lot of lay people mean when they mean happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以，享乐主义的快乐，我认为是很多外行人在提到快乐时所指的意思。

sentences.en: That's just like a sense of good feeling, right?
sentences.zh: 那就像是一种良好的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: That's your personal pleasure.
sentences.zh: 那是你的个人愉悦。

sentences.en: That's like the difference between eating a hot fudge sundae or stubbing your toe, right?
sentences.zh: 那就像吃热软糖圣代和踢到脚趾之间的区别，对吧？

sentences.en: Like there's something that it feels like to feel like things are good.
sentences.zh: 就像感觉一切都很好，那种感觉是真实存在的。

sentences.en: And often when we're thinking of hedonic pleasure, we're thinking of the real basic stuff that evolution built in, you know, good food, good sex, a feeling of, like,
sentences.zh: 通常当我们想到享乐时，我们想到的是进化内置的那些非常基本的东西，你知道，好的食物、好的性生活、一种成就感，

sentences.en: accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 就像，

sentences.en: Like, these are the things that matter for us.
sentences.zh: 这些是对我们重要的事情。

sentences.en: Eudaimonic happiness is bigger.
sentences.zh: 幸福主义的快乐则更宏大。

sentences.en: It's really about living a good life.
sentences.zh: 它真正关乎的是过上一种美好的生活。

sentences.en: It's about happiness that comes not just from your own success, your own pleasure, but from other people, from, like, actually building character.
sentences.zh: 这种快乐不仅来自你自己的成功、你自己的愉悦，还来自他人，来自真正地塑造品格。

sentences.en: And if you look back at the ancients, folks like Aristotle and so on, they knew about both.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾古代，像亚里士多德等人，他们对两者都有所了解。

sentences.en: But when push came to shove, they were like, go for the eudaimonic happiness, right?
sentences.zh: 但当关键时刻来临时，他们会说，去追求幸福主义的快乐吧，对吧？

sentences.en: That is really, it's really about.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正重要的。

sentences.en: They thought of like happiness as really synonymous with building character, doing nice stuff for others, civic virtue.
sentences.zh: 他们认为快乐实际上等同于塑造品格、为他人做好事、具有公民美德。

sentences.en: It was much more like happiness as virtue.
sentences.zh: 这更像是作为美德的快乐。

sentences.en: And when you look at the modern science, like this tension comes up, right?
sentences.zh: 当你审视现代科学时，这种张力就会出现，对吧？

sentences.en: And a lot of the interventions I talk about with my students, and maybe we'll even talk about today, there's a real question about which type of happiness we're building up.
sentences.zh: 我与学生讨论的许多干预措施，也许我们今天也会讨论，关于我们正在建立哪种类型的快乐，这确实是一个问题。

sentences.en: And I think where the research falls is saying that, like, if we want to do this well, we should probably be going more for the eudaimonic stuff.
sentences.zh: 我认为研究得出的结论是，如果我们想做好这件事，我们可能应该更多地追求幸福主义的东西。

sentences.en: Like, that's the stuff we don't get used to.
sentences.zh: 因为那是我们不会产生适应性的东西。

sentences.en: That's the stuff where we get kind of more bang for our buck in terms of interventions and time and so on.
sentences.zh: 那是我们在干预措施和时间等方面能获得更多回报的东西。

sentences.en: But all too often, when you look on the internet, if you look at social media influencers, when they're talking about happiness, they usually mean the hedonic stuff.
sentences.zh: 但太频繁地，当你在互联网上查看时，如果你看社交媒体网红，当他们谈论快乐时，他们通常指的是享乐主义的东西。

sentences.en: And that's great.
sentences.zh: 那也很好。

sentences.en: I mean, it's great to have, you know, great sex and hot fudge sundaes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拥有很棒的性生活和热软糖圣代是很棒的。

sentences.en: But ultimately, you know, true happiness probably comes from what we do with others and building a broader good life.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，你知道，真正的快乐可能来自我们与他人的互动以及建立更广阔的美好生活。

sentences.en: In ancient Greece, the big philosophical debate was also if happiness is nature or nurture.
sentences.zh: 在古希腊，重大的哲学辩论还在于快乐是天生的还是后天培养的。

sentences.en: What does the science say?
sentences.zh: 科学是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Are certain people more predisposed to be happy?
sentences.zh: 某些人是否天生就更容易快乐？

sentences.en: Is it biological?
sentences.zh: 这是生物学决定的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the way scientists study this is they do these classic studies with twins.
sentences.zh: 科学家研究这个问题的方法是进行经典的双胞胎研究。

sentences.en: And the reason scientists are so obsessed with twins is that you get two kinds of twins.
sentences.zh: 科学家如此痴迷于双胞胎的原因是你可以得到两种双胞胎。

sentences.en: You get identical twins who are genetic clones of one another.
sentences.zh: 你有同卵双胞胎，他们是彼此的基因克隆。

sentences.en: And you also have fraternal twins who are as related as regular siblings, but they were in the same womb.
sentences.zh: 你也有异卵双胞胎，他们的亲缘关系就像普通兄弟姐妹一样，但他们在同一个子宫里，

sentences.en: They probably grew up the same way and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们可能以同样的方式长大等等。

sentences.en: And so what scientists do is they say, well, if there's a genetic component to happiness, if something about the variants that we see in the population is controlled by our genes,
sentences.zh: 所以科学家们会说，好吧，如果快乐有遗传成分，如果我们在人群中看到的变异中有某些部分是由我们的基因控制的，

sentences.en: then those identical twins should look more similar in terms of their happiness than the fraternal twins.
sentences.zh: 那么同卵双胞胎在快乐程度上应该比异卵双胞胎看起来更相似。

sentences.en: And like lots of studies have looked at this.
sentences.zh: 很多研究都关注了这一点。

sentences.en: And what they generally find is that happiness is heritable.
sentences.zh: 他们通常发现快乐是可以遗传的。

sentences.en: In other words, that doesn't mean there's a gene for happiness or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这并不意味着有一个“快乐基因”之类的东西。

sentences.en: That means that some of the variants that we see in the population is due to the fact that somebody has one set of genetics versus another set of genetics.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们在人群中看到的一些变异，是因为某人拥有一套基因，而另一个人拥有另一套基因。

sentences.en: The important thing to know about those heritability studies, though, is that the heritability factor is pretty low.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于这些遗传力研究，重要的一点是，遗传力因素相当低。

sentences.en: It's about the same rate as what you'd see for the heritability of something like religiosity or risk-taking, right?
sentences.zh: 它大约和你看到的宗教信仰或冒险精神的遗传率处于同一水平，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, religiosity is probably, you know, if your parents were super religious, maybe you're more likely to be super religious, but obviously it's not set in stone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，宗教信仰可能，你知道，如果你的父母非常虔诚，也许你更有可能非常虔诚，但这显然不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: Same thing with risk taking.
sentences.zh: 冒险精神也是如此。

sentences.en: And I think that's the message of happiness.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是关于快乐的信息。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's probably some component that's a little built in, but so much more of it is under our conscious control.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能有一些内置的成分，但更多的是在我们的意识控制之下。

sentences.en: So we can learn to be happy?
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以学会快乐吗？

sentences.en: I think that's the premise of my work, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这就是我工作的核心前提。

sentences.en: It's that we have much more control over it.
sentences.zh: 我们对它有更多的控制权。

sentences.en: And interestingly, this was something that the ancient Greeks didn't totally realize.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这是古希腊人并没有完全意识到的事情。

sentences.en: You know, if you look at Aristotle, he's like, we should cultivate virtue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你看亚里士多德，他说我们应该培养美德。

sentences.en: you can do it, but it's going to be hard.
sentences.zh: 你可以做到，但这会很难。

sentences.en: You know, Aristotle talked about the happy few.
sentences.zh: 你知道，亚里士多德谈到了“快乐的少数人”。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, you can go for it, but it's going to take a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，你可以去追求它，但这需要付出很多努力。

sentences.en: And probably a lot of folks aren't going to be up for that level of work.
sentences.zh: 而且可能很多人不会愿意付出那种程度的努力。

sentences.en: I think we think it's a little bit more malleable scientifically today, but we still share with Aristotle this idea that like, if you want to be happy, you can do it.
sentences.zh: 我认为今天我们在科学上认为它更具可塑性，但我们仍然与亚里士多德有着共同的观点，即如果你想快乐，你可以做到。

sentences.en: But like all good things in life, you got to put some time in.
sentences.zh: 但就像生活中所有美好的事物一样，你必须投入时间。

sentences.en: When we think about happiness or well-being, is there a goal or is it just in the way that Aristotle said an endless pursuit?
sentences.zh: 当我们思考快乐或幸福时，有一个目标吗？还是就像亚里士多德所说的那样，是一种无止境的追求？

sentences.en: I mean, can we reach the mountaintop and we just sit there or is it just
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们能到达山顶然后就坐在那里吗？还是说它只是

sentences.en: always searching for that place?
sentences.zh: 一直在寻找那个地方？

sentences.en: The pursuit of happiness is not like a destination.
sentences.zh: 对快乐的追求不是一个目的地。

sentences.en: Like if I hopped on a flight and I got to L.A., if I hopped on a flight to get to L.A., I'd just be in L.A.
sentences.zh: 就像如果我跳上一架飞机到达洛杉矶，如果我跳上一架飞机去洛杉矶，我就只是在洛杉矶了。

sentences.en: I'd be like, all right, LA, I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我会觉得，好吧，洛杉矶，我到了。

sentences.en: If I had the ability to stay, I could just stay there for a whole time.
sentences.zh: 如果我有能力留下来，我可以一直待在那里。

sentences.en: But happiness doesn't work like that.
sentences.zh: 但快乐不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: It's not really a destination.
sentences.zh: 它真的不是一个目的地。

sentences.en: And I think that it's funny when we think about happiness, because I think we do kind of think of it as a destination, but we don't think of that with other good things in life.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得当我们思考快乐时很有趣，因为我认为我们确实把它看作是一个目的地，但我们不会那样看待生活中其他美好的事物。

sentences.en: Take fitness.
sentences.zh: 以健身为例。

sentences.en: Say you're trying to get fit.
sentences.zh: 假设你正在努力变得健康。

sentences.en: I'm going to go to the gym.
sentences.zh: 我要去健身房。

sentences.en: It would be awesome if you took one really hard HIIT class, and then you were just good.
sentences.zh: 如果你上了一节非常高强度的HIIT课，然后你就一直保持良好状态，那会很棒。

sentences.en: You did that in your 20s, and then all through midlife.
sentences.zh: 你在20多岁时做了这件事，然后整个中年时期，

sentences.en: You're like, I took my HIIT class.
sentences.zh: 你觉得，我上过我的HIIT课了。

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我状态很好。

sentences.en: Fitness was a destination.
sentences.zh: 健身是一个目的地。

sentences.en: No, we kind of get like, you got to keep doing it over time or those kind of benefits don't stick.

sentences.en: And I had my young daughter and she would go to the beach every day and I had good friends.
sentences.zh: 我有年幼的女儿，她每天都会去海滩，我也有好朋友。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not even like looking back, I was happy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，甚至不是回顾过去，我当时就是快乐的。

sentences.en: I knew at the time that I was experiencing sort of happiness.

sentences.zh: 实际上有关于此的研究，如果你观察普通人所指的含义，他们往往指的是一种特定的幸福感。

sentences.en: And it's kind of the one that you're getting at, which is sort of being happy in your life, which we might think of as like an affective part of happiness.
sentences.zh: 这正是你所提到的那种，即在生活中感到快乐，我们可以将其视为幸福感中的情感部分。

sentences.en: You're just experiencing lots of positive emotions, right?
sentences.zh: 你只是在体验大量的积极情绪，对吧？

sentences.en: It's awesome to live in Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 住在里约热内卢真是太棒了。

sentences.en: It's awesome to stick your feet in the sand.
sentences.zh: 把脚埋进沙子里感觉真好。

sentences.en: Like that just feels good.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉真的很棒。

sentences.en: And that's half of, I think, what social scientists mean when they talk about happiness.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是社会科学家在谈论幸福时所指的一半含义。

sentences.en: They're talking about the feeling, how it feels to be in your life.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是那种感觉，即你在生活中感受如何。

sentences.en: It's kind of the ratio of your positive to negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是你积极情绪与消极情绪的比例。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get into this, but happiness isn't about getting rid of your negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 也许我们稍后会深入探讨，但幸福并不是要消除你的消极情绪。

sentences.en: That's not what social scientists mean.
sentences.zh: 那不是社会科学家所指的意思。

sentences.en: But it really is about having a decent ratio between the positive to negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 但它确实关乎在积极情绪和消极情绪之间保持一个合理的比例。

sentences.en: That's kind of being happy in your life.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的在生活中感到快乐。

sentences.en: But happiness, according to social scientists, has a second component too, which is this idea of being happy with your life.
sentences.zh: 但根据社会科学家的说法，幸福还有第二个组成部分，即对生活感到满意的理念。

sentences.en: And that gets more towards these eudaimoniaic components.
sentences.zh: 这更接近于“幸福感”（eudaimoniaic）的范畴。

sentences.en: That's that you're satisfied with your life.
sentences.zh: 那就是你对自己的生活感到满足。

sentences.en: You have a sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 你有一种意义感。

sentences.en: You have a sense of purpose.
sentences.zh: 你有一种目标感。

sentences.en: It feels good to be you because of how you think it's going.
sentences.zh: 因为你觉得生活进展顺利，所以做你自己感觉很好。

sentences.en: So this is kind of a cognitive part of happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以这是幸福感中认知层面的部分。

sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们试图以正确的方式追求幸福时，理论上我们应该努力提升这两者。

sentences.zh: 这就是你所反对的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's really summed up by the phrase that you see on social media all the time of good vibes only.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可以用你在社交媒体上随处可见的短语“只传递正能量”来概括。

sentences.en: Like, good vibes only.
sentences.zh: 就像，“只传递正能量”。

sentences.en: If there are any bad vibes, something's really off, right?
sentences.zh: 如果出现任何负面情绪，就觉得哪里不对劲，对吧？

sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Like when I talk to my students, the way I often talk about negative emotions is as a signal, just like other negative sensations, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我和学生交谈时，我通常把消极情绪描述为一种信号，就像其他负面感觉一样，对吧？

sentences.en: You put your hand on a really hot stove, it's going to hurt.
sentences.zh: 如果你把手放在很烫的炉子上，它会疼。

sentences.en: It's going to burn.

sentences.zh: 你之所以有那种感觉，是因为它是一个很好的信号。

sentences.en: It's like, get your hand off that stove.
sentences.zh: 它就像是在说，快把手从炉子上拿开。

sentences.en: So many of our negative emotions are doing that for us.
sentences.zh: 我们许多消极情绪都在为我们做同样的事。

sentences.en: We should be so grateful for them because they're helping us, right?
sentences.zh: 我们应该对它们心存感激，因为它们在帮助我们，对吧？

sentences.en: If I'm feeling lonely, that's a signal that I need to change my behavior.
sentences.zh: 如果我感到孤独，那是一个信号，说明我需要改变我的行为。

sentences.en: I need to seek out some social connection.
sentences.zh: 我需要寻求一些社交联系。

sentences.en: If I'm feeling sad, that's a signal that something's amiss, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我感到悲伤，那是一个信号，说明有什么事情不对劲，对吧？

sentences.en: I might need more positive things in my life.
sentences.zh: 我的生活中可能需要更多积极的事物。

sentences.en: A big one for me that I noticed myself is if I'm feeling overwhelmed, that means I have way too much on my plate, right?
sentences.zh: 对我个人而言，我注意到的一大信号是，如果我感到不知所措，那意味着我承担的事情太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: I have to make some changes.
sentences.zh: 我必须做出一些改变。

sentences.en: And those are signals, just like the signal we get from a hand on a hot stove, that to get back to equilibrium, we need to make some changes.
sentences.zh: 这些都是信号，就像手放在热炉子上得到的信号一样，为了回到平衡状态，我们需要做出一些改变。

sentences.en: And it would be sad to get rid of those.
sentences.zh: 如果摆脱这些情绪，那才令人悲哀。

sentences.en: If you only had good vibes only, I feel like you couldn't live a positive life because you'd be missing out on these cues about where you're going
sentences.zh: 如果你只想要“正能量”，我觉得你无法过上积极的生活，因为你会错过这些关于你何时偏离轨道以及应该做出何种改变的线索。

sentences.en: off track and what you should change.
sentences.zh: 偏离了轨道，以及你应该做出什么改变。

sentences.zh: 你是否担心这种追求幸福、总是渴望更多的想法，实际上反而制造了不幸福？

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对会。

sentences.en: California at Berkeley.

sentences.en: so i don't know you go on some really cool trip to rio de janeiro and you're like i'm annoyed with the sand, like it's a little too sunny.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，你去里约热内卢进行了一次很酷的旅行，然后你却觉得“我对沙子感到厌烦，阳光太刺眼了”。

sentences.zh: 我感觉不到快乐。

sentences.zh: 这是第一种情绪。

sentences.zh: 但随后元情绪就出现了。

sentences.en: You're ashamed.
sentences.zh: 你感到羞愧。

sentences.zh: 我怎么能在里约热内卢却感觉不到快乐呢？

sentences.en: You're disappointed, like, oh, I spent all this money on this stuff.
sentences.zh: 你感到失望，比如，哦，我在这上面花了很多钱。

sentences.zh: 你在评判自己。

sentences.zh: 我为什么感觉不好，我出了什么问题？

sentences.zh: 每当我们觉得偏离了追求幸福的道路时，这些情绪就会出现。

sentences.en: so yeah it really does seem empirically that it's a paradox right that the more we go after

sentences.en: vibes only the more we kind of don't ever get there key though is that the paradox doesn't come up as much if you're pursuing the healthier kind of happiness?
sentences.zh: 关键在于，如果你追求的是更健康的幸福，这种悖论就不会那么明显，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, when I was thinking about this, initially I was like, oh, this is such a modern idea, this idea of happiness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我思考这个问题时，起初我觉得，哦，这真是一个现代的想法，这种关于幸福的观念。

sentences.en: You know, this pursuit of happiness is something that I'm sure they didn't care about in the Middle Ages when they were struggling to eat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种对幸福的追求，我相信在中世纪人们挣扎着填饱肚子时，他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: They weren't worried about, you know, maximizing their sense of joy and aspiration to live the good life.
sentences.zh: 他们并不担心，你知道，最大化他们的快乐感和对美好生活的向往。

sentences.en: And then I was sort of struck by the fact that this has been something very human for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 然后我被一个事实所触动，那就是这在很长一段时间里都是非常人性化的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we have cared about happiness for as long as we've been humans and could reflect on our own emotions and reflect
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为只要我们是人类，能够反思自己的情绪，反思

sentences.en: on the state of being a human and what it means to be a human.
sentences.zh: 身为人类的状态以及身为人类意味着什么，我们就一直关心幸福。

sentences.en: But I think cultures really shift how we think about what we should be doing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为文化确实改变了我们对应该做什么的看法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think if you look at most of human history, sorry, I'm going to nerd out and do like a happiness history lesson.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为如果你回顾大多数人类历史，抱歉，我要开始掉书袋，上一堂幸福历史课了。

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: If you look at most of human history, we just didn't think it was possible to pursue happiness.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾大多数人类历史，我们根本不认为追求幸福是可能的。

sentences.en: So the word happiness comes from the cognate of luck.
sentences.zh: 所以“幸福”（happiness）这个词源于“运气”（luck）的同源词。

sentences.en: It's hap, right?
sentences.zh: 是“hap”，对吧？

sentences.en: Like happenstance.
sentences.zh: 就像“偶然”（happenstance）。

sentences.en: You know, I think even Shakespeare said, hap what hap may or something like that, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想连莎士比亚都说过，“随遇而安”（hap what hap may）之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, it's just luck.
sentences.zh: 就像，这只是运气。

sentences.en: You might get a boulder might fall on your head or it might not, but you can't control that, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能会被一块巨石砸中，也可能不会，但你无法控制这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: That is for most of human history how we thought about happiness.
sentences.zh: 在大多数人类历史中，我们就是这样看待幸福的。

sentences.en: Like, it's good if you get it, but like, you can't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 就像，得到了固然好，但你对此无能为力。

sentences.en: Then we get to the classic Greeks, right?
sentences.zh: 然后我们到了古希腊时期，对吧？

sentences.en: Folks like Aristotle and others.
sentences.zh: 像亚里士多德和其他人那样的人。

sentences.en: And they had a slightly different view.
sentences.zh: 他们有稍微不同的看法。

sentences.en: They also thought, you know, it's got a lot to do with luck and so on, but you can actually go for it.
sentences.zh: 他们也认为，你知道，这与运气等有很大关系，但你实际上可以去争取它。

sentences.en: If you try to build up your virtue, if you try to go for that eudaimonic happiness, then you will get closer to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你努力培养美德，如果你努力去追求那种“幸福感”（eudaimonic happiness），那么你就会更接近它。

sentences.en: You might not.

sentences.en: You might not get there, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能达不到，对吧？

sentences.en: The happy other happy few, but you can try.
sentences.zh: 那些少数幸运儿，但你可以尝试。

sentences.en: And I think we had that classic notion for a long time until we get to more of the modern day, until we get to the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们长期以来一直持有这种经典观念，直到进入现代，直到18世纪。

sentences.en: And that was where a few things started to change in these really interesting ways, right?

sentences.en: One is that this is the first time where we're not having all the like Middle Ages stuff that you were just talking about, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，这是我们第一次不再经历你刚才谈到的那些中世纪的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: This is less 18th century, again, a little less pestilence, a little less terrible stuff going on.
sentences.zh: 这已经不是18世纪了，瘟疫少了，可怕的事情也少了。

sentences.en: Life is starting to feel more controllable, like even in really stupid ways, right?
sentences.zh: 生活开始感觉更可控了，即使是以非常愚蠢的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: They could control the smoke that was coming out of their chimneys.
sentences.zh: 他们可以控制烟囱里冒出的烟。

sentences.en: They made bedding that was like a little bit softer.
sentences.zh: 他们制作了稍微柔软一点的寝具。

sentences.en: They had better lighting in their houses, right?
sentences.zh: 他们房子里的照明更好了，对吧？

sentences.en: Better food.
sentences.zh: 更好的食物。

sentences.en: Better food, right?
sentences.zh: 更好的食物，对吧？

sentences.en: It started to feel like, oh, I can – it's reasonable to think I might be able to control my hedonic happiness because I've seen some evidence that my actions can do that.
sentences.zh: 开始感觉，哦，我可以——认为我或许能控制我的享乐主义幸福是合理的，因为我已经看到了一些证据表明我的行为可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: And at the same time, you get cultural changes that fit with this, right?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你也会看到与之相适应的文化变革，对吧？

sentences.zh: 这大约是艾萨克·牛顿等人所处的科学时代，我们了解到物体只是以特定的方式运动。

sentences.en: Gravity pushes objects towards one another.
sentences.zh: 重力将物体推向彼此。

sentences.en: Scientists are also starting to think, well, what does that mean for humans?
sentences.zh: 科学家们也开始思考，这对人类意味着什么？

sentences.en: Oh, we move towards pleasure and away from pain.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们趋向快乐，远离痛苦。

sentences.zh: 这些就像杰里米·边沁（Jeremy Bentham）关于这些东西的论点。

sentences.en: So the idea is like, oh, we're built to seek out pleasure.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，哦，我们天生就是为了寻求快乐。

sentences.en: Like, this is a thing we should go for.
sentences.zh: 就像，这是我们应该追求的东西。

sentences.en: So yeah, so I think every generation has wanted to feel happy.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我认为每一代人都想感到快乐。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, you know, Bentham was right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，你知道，边沁是对的。

sentences.en: We are built to pursue pleasure and avoid pain.
sentences.zh: 我们天生就是为了追求快乐和避免痛苦。

sentences.en: But the cultural context in which we think about that can be different over time.
sentences.zh: 但我们思考这一点的文化背景会随着时间的推移而改变。

sentences.en: We are in the notion of like, it looks maxing, like, you know, like getting all your pleasure right now and, you know, spa pedicures and this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于一种“颜值至上”的观念中，就像，你知道，现在就获取所有的快乐，还有水疗修脚之类的东西。

sentences.en: I think we really just definitionally think of happiness as about me, me, me.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从定义上真的把幸福看作是关于“我，我，我”。

sentences.en: And so much of the science and so much of this classic wisdom tells us, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 而大量的科学研究和许多经典智慧告诉我们，不，并不是这样。

sentences.en: Like, that's the way you get off track.
sentences.zh: 那是你偏离轨道的方式。

sentences.en: That's the way you pursue it in the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 那是你以错误方式追求它的方式。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So that brings us to what we deal with today.
sentences.zh: 所以这把我们带到了今天所面临的问题。

sentences.en: And I really want to focus on social connection because the pandemic, I think, showed us that if you don't have it, you're really,
sentences.zh: 我真的想关注社交联系，因为我认为疫情向我们表明，如果你没有它，你真的，

sentences.en: really going to suffer in ways that were perhaps not clear.
sentences.zh: 真的会以某种或许不那么明显的方式受苦。

sentences.en: and I have been trying to figure out what happened to me during that period, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我一直在试图弄清楚在那段时期我身上发生了什么。

sentences.en: I became a lot more insular and I had to sort of relearn how to make those social connections after that period.
sentences.zh: 我变得更加封闭，在那之后我不得不重新学习如何建立那些社交联系。

sentences.en: Am I typical?
sentences.zh: 我是典型的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, no studies bear this out.
sentences.zh: 是的，没有研究能证明这一点。

sentences.en: Pretty much every survey I know of that asks people about COVID, like, was it smooth sailing when you jump back into it?
sentences.zh: 我所知道的几乎每一项询问人们关于新冠疫情的调查，比如，当你重新开始社交时，一切是否顺利？

sentences.en: People are like, no, right?
sentences.zh: 人们的回答是，不，对吧？

sentences.en: There was some friction to this.
sentences.zh: 这其中存在一些摩擦。

sentences.en: We kind of got out of practice from it.
sentences.zh: 我们有点生疏了。

sentences.en: And that makes sense because even though we're built to be social, right, even though in some sense this should be easy, social connection is hard, right?
sentences.zh: 这说得通，因为尽管我们天生就是社会性的，对吧，尽管在某种意义上这应该很容易，但社交联系其实很难，对吧？

sentences.en: There's another mind there that you're trying to like navigate and predict and you don't often get direct access to it.
sentences.zh: 那里有另一个思想，你试图去引导和预测它，而你通常无法直接接触到它。

sentences.en: So it is clunky, and it does have some friction.
sentences.zh: 所以它很笨拙，确实有一些摩擦。

sentences.en: That friction is one of the reasons that, you know, as a professor, whenever I go into the dining hall, I'm shocked at how few of my students are just talking to one another.
sentences.zh: 这种摩擦是原因之一，你知道，作为一名教授，每当我走进餐厅，看到很少有学生在互相交谈，我都很震惊。

sentences.en: This is something professors remark about now when I walk into my classroom, say a seminar room, where all my students are sitting around a table.
sentences.zh: 这是教授们现在谈论的事情，当我走进教室，比如研讨室，我所有的学生都坐在桌子旁。

sentences.en: They're not chatting with one another.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在互相聊天。

sentences.en: They're all on a screen looking at it.
sentences.zh: 他们都在屏幕前看着它。

sentences.en: And I think the problem for them is there's a little bit of friction.
sentences.zh: 我认为对他们来说，问题在于存在一点点阻力。

sentences.en: It's hard to get that going.
sentences.zh: 很难让它运转起来。

sentences.en: And when you didn't do it for a year, a year and a half, however long it was, yeah, it got harder.
sentences.zh: 当你有一年、一年半，或者无论多久没有这样做时，是的，它变得更难了。

sentences.en: You were simply out of practice from it.
sentences.zh: 你只是因为疏于练习而变得生疏了。

sentences.en: And I actually think that this is one of the reasons that our young people, I mentioned my students, are so lonely right now, is I think just like over their developmental time,
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为这是我们的年轻人——我提到了我的学生——现在如此孤独的原因之一，我认为就像在他们的成长过程中，

sentences.en: they just had less practice at it.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面的练习变少了。

sentences.en: Like the modern world is taking away all these subtle ways that we talk to one another.
sentences.zh: 现代世界正在剥夺我们彼此交流的那些微妙方式。

sentences.en: One of my favorite articles that looked at this was by the Talking Heads frontman, David Byrne.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的探讨这一点的文章之一，是由“传声头像”乐队（Talking Heads）的主唱大卫·伯恩（David Byrne）写的。

sentences.en: He wrote this article kind of presciently, I think this was back in the 2010s, called Eliminating the Human.
sentences.zh: 他写这篇文章时很有预见性，我想那是在2010年代，题目叫《消除人类》（Eliminating the Human）。

sentences.en: And his idea was like, if you look at what pretty much every technology has done, it's taken away the human from something as simple as like, we go to the ATM now.
sentences.zh: 他的观点是，如果你看看几乎所有技术所做的事情，它都在消除人类的参与，比如我们现在去自动取款机（ATM）取钱。

sentences.en: We don't have to talk to a teller.
sentences.zh: 我们不必与柜员交谈。

sentences.en: We don't go to a record store and talk with people about records to get our music.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去唱片店与人讨论唱片来获取音乐。

sentences.en: We just have an algorithm deliver it to us.
sentences.zh: 我们只是让算法把它推送给我们。

sentences.en: in all these subtle ways our technologies are making it so that we don't need to like talk to regular people and i think we forget like the subtle ways that this keeps coming up
sentences.zh: 在所有这些微妙的方面，我们的技术正在让我们不再需要与普通人交谈，我认为我们忘记了这种影响是如何不断显现的。

sentences.en: what do you think ai is going to do because they really is trying to eliminate the human
sentences.zh: 你认为人工智能会做什么？因为它确实在试图消除人类。

sentences.en: yeah no it's going to get way worse because the friction of talking to an lm i mean we're already
sentences.zh: 是的，不，情况会变得更糟，因为与大语言模型（LLM）交谈的阻力——我的意思是，我们已经

sentences.en: seeing this isn't there the llm is there whenever you want to talk right if you're feeling up at two in the morning, you can say that.
sentences.zh: 看到了这一点，不是吗？只要你想聊，大语言模型就在那里，对吧？如果你在凌晨两点感到心烦，你可以跟它说。

sentences.en: The LLM is really not judgy.
sentences.zh: 大语言模型真的不会评判你。

sentences.en: You know, if anything, the current iterations, when you and I are having this conversation, we're learning are too sycophantic, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果说有什么的话，目前的版本——当我们进行这段对话时——我们了解到它们太会阿谀奉承了，对吧？

sentences.en: They can almost create cognitive delusions in people.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎可以在人们心中制造认知错觉。

sentences.en: But yet, that is what our young people are turning to.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我们的年轻人所转向的对象。

sentences.en: I just had Jean Twenge, the kind of technology specialist on our podcast, who's talked a lot about phones.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚邀请了技术专家简·特温格（Jean Twenge）上我们的播客，她谈了很多关于手机的问题。

sentences.en: And she's really shifting to the dangers of AI.
sentences.zh: 她现在真的转向关注人工智能的危险性了。

sentences.en: One of her data points is just how many young people, and we're talking like 12, 13-year-olds, are having their first relationship with an LLM.
sentences.zh: 她的一个数据点是，有多少年轻人——我们指的是12、13岁的孩子——正在与大语言模型建立他们的第一段关系。

sentences.en: Like their first boyfriend and girlfriend is an LLM.
sentences.zh: 就像他们的第一个男朋友或女朋友是一个大语言模型。

sentences.en: And so what's the friction going to look like when they have to ask a real human out on a date, navigate like a sexual consent conversation
sentences.zh: 那么，当他们不得不约一个真实的人出去约会，处理像性同意这样的对话时，阻力会是什么样子？

sentences.en: with a real other human with preferences and so on?
sentences.zh: 与一个有偏好等等的真实人类进行互动？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think AI is going to change this in ways that are likely to make it worse.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为人工智能会以可能使其变得更糟的方式改变这一点。

sentences.en: It creates this cycle where it becomes harder and harder to overcome that little friction to talk to someone.
sentences.zh: 它创造了一个循环，使得克服与人交谈的那一点点阻力变得越来越难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, my daughter asked me recently, how do you start a conversation with strangers?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我女儿最近问我，你如何与陌生人开启对话？

sentences.en: How do you go up to someone that you don't know and just start to talk to them?
sentences.zh: 你如何走到一个你不认识的人面前，直接开始和他们说话？

sentences.en: And of course, that's a function of their age and that's totally normal.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是他们年龄的一个特征，这完全正常。

sentences.en: I mean, they're learning how to interact in the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们正在学习如何在这个世界上互动。

sentences.en: But I also realize, like, how much harder it is to do that nowadays because you're not only interrupting maybe a social dynamic,
sentences.zh: 但我同时也意识到，如今这样做有多难，因为你不仅可能打断了一种社交动态，

sentences.en: you're also interrupting people's interaction with their devices.
sentences.zh: 你还在打断人们与他们设备之间的互动。

sentences.en: And I notice that in my own family because she comes up to me and I'm on my phone and I feel annoyed sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我在我自己的家庭中也注意到了这一点，因为她走到我面前时，我正在看手机，有时我会感到烦躁。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, I'm in the middle of reading.
sentences.zh: 我会说，噢，我正在阅读呢。

sentences.en: Can't you see?
sentences.zh: 你没看见吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so all these cues that it's appropriate to talk to someone, right, that they're making eye contact with you, they're smiling with you.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些暗示可以与人交谈的线索，对吧，比如他们与你进行眼神交流，他们对你微笑。

sentences.en: That doesn't happen when your eyes are glued to your phone.
sentences.zh: 当你的眼睛盯着手机时，这一切都不会发生。

sentences.en: And there's such interesting research on this.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有非常有趣的研究。

sentences.en: Liz Dunn, who's a professor at the University of British Columbia, has a study I love where she puts people in a waiting room, strangers in a waiting room,
sentences.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚大学的教授莉兹·邓恩（Liz Dunn）有一项我非常喜欢的研究，她把陌生人放在一个候诊室里，

sentences.en: and just either has them have access to their phones or not.
sentences.zh: 让他们有的能用手机，有的不能。

sentences.en: And she just measures a really creative dependent variable, which is how often they spontaneously smile at each other.
sentences.zh: 她测量了一个非常有创意的因变量，那就是他们自发地对彼此微笑的频率。

sentences.en: You're sitting there, you just look over and smile.
sentences.zh: 你坐在那里，只是抬头看一眼然后微笑。

sentences.en: 30% decrease in smiling.
sentences.zh: 微笑减少了30%。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Multiply that by what's happening on the streets of New York, right?
sentences.zh: 把这个乘以在纽约街头发生的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: What's happening in New York.
sentences.zh: 在纽约发生的事情。

sentences.en: Let's not use New York.
sentences.zh: 我们别拿纽约举例了。

sentences.en: New York people are never smiling in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约人在纽约从不微笑。

sentences.en: Well, it's happening in Boston.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这在波士顿也在发生。

sentences.en: It happens in Boston too.
sentences.zh: 波士顿也一样。

sentences.en: I mean, what's happening at your own dinner table, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你自己的餐桌上发生了什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Where your daughter is about to tell you something about your day, but your eyes are glued to your phone, right?
sentences.zh: 当你的女儿正要告诉你关于她一天的事情，但你的眼睛却盯着手机，对吧？

sentences.en: She talks about it all the time.
sentences.zh: 她一直在谈论这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you just don't notice, right?
sentences.zh: 而你根本没注意到，对吧？

sentences.en: And, you know, we're not like harshing on people for their phones.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们并不是在严厉批评人们使用手机。

sentences.en: Like, they're built to be interesting.
sentences.zh: 它们被设计得很有趣。

sentences.en: They're built to have every interesting thing in the history of the universe.
sentences.zh: 它们被设计成拥有宇宙历史上每一件有趣的事情。

sentences.en: But the consequence of our eyeballs being glued to them is really dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但我们的眼球被粘在它们上面的后果真的很危险。

sentences.en: dangerous for the social connections we care about moSt.
sentences.zh: 对于我们最关心的社会联系来说很危险。

sentences.en: I mean, this speaks to the wider situation in which we find ourselves, because I was looking at some data from 2012 to now, and there was a recent report by the American
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这说明了我们所处的更广泛的情况，因为我查看了从2012年到现在的一些数据，美国企业研究所（American Enterprise Institute）最近有一份报告显示，在所有年龄段中，人们现在与邻居的社交活动都在减少。

sentences.en: Enterprise Institute that shows that across all age groups, people are now socializing with their neighbors less.
sentences.zh: 作者归咎于很多因素，比如技术、政治极化、大流行后的问题。

sentences.en: And the authors blame a lot of things like technology, political polarization, post-pandemic issues.
sentences.zh: 但你认为我们作为一个国家，是否已经变成了室内猫而不是室外猫？

sentences.en: But do you think we've just become sort of as a nation, indoor cats instead of outdoor cats?
sentences.zh: 就像我们已经失去了在野外漫游的能力？

sentences.en: Like we just have lost the ability to roam in the wild?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这有一定道理。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there's something to that.
sentences.zh: 这是学者们担心已久的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: And this is something that scholars have been worried about for a while, right?
sentences.zh: 回溯到90年代末、2000年代初。

sentences.en: Rewind the late 90s, early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·普特南（Robert Putnam）那本关于《独自打保龄球》（Bowling Alone）的开创性著作，他在书中论证说

sentences.en: And you have Robert Putnam's like seminal book on bowling alone, where he argued like
sentences.zh: 过去，我们会去保龄球馆，人们会和朋友一起打球，一起打球，参加联赛。

sentences.en: Back in the day, we'd go out to bowling alleys and people would bowl with their friends and bowl together and bowl in leagues.
sentences.zh: 如今——这里的如今指的是2000年代初——人们只是去独自打球，对吧？

sentences.en: Nowadays, or nowadays being early 2000s, nowadays people just go and they bowl alone, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不是联赛的一部分。

sentences.en: They're not part of a league.
sentences.zh: 他们没有和邻居交谈。

sentences.en: They're not talking to their neighbors.
sentences.zh: 他们只和身边的朋友交谈。

sentences.en: They just talk to their immediate friends.
sentences.zh: 我为我的播客采访过罗伯特·普特南，你知道，他有一个很有趣的想法，他说，你知道，我在那之前写了那本书。

sentences.en: I talked with Robert Putnam for my podcast, you know, and he had this interesting idea of like, you know, I wrote that before.
sentences.zh: 那时互联网还处于婴儿期。

sentences.en: Like the internet was like in baby days.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道病毒式传播的TikTok视频即将到来，对吧？

sentences.en: Like we didn't know that like viral TikTok videos were coming, right?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道还有电视，那是他当时担心的，对吧？

sentences.en: We didn't know that there was television, which he was worried about, right?
sentences.zh: 那是他谈到的因素之一。

sentences.en: That was one of the factors he talked about.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道会有流媒体服务，它们通过算法为你精准推送只有你——露露（Lulu）——才会喜欢的最佳纪录片，对吧？

sentences.en: But we didn't know there was going to be like, you know, streaming services that picked algorithms to get you exactly the best documentary that only you, Lulu, would love, right?
sentences.zh: 我们正在与那些让事物变得有趣和吸引人的技术作斗争。

sentences.en: We're fighting against technology that makes stuff interesting and attractive.
sentences.zh: 有整个公司都是为了让我们的眼球盯着那些东西而建立的。

sentences.en: Like there are whole companies that are built to keep our eyeballs on that stuff.
sentences.zh: 当然，在那种竞争面前，我在保龄球馆与朋友的常规社交联系可能会受到影响。

sentences.en: Of course, regular social connection with my friend at the bowling alley might suffer, like in the face of that kind of competition.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也和罗伯特·普特南谈过，他的处方简而言之就是：加入一个俱乐部，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I also spoke to Robert Putnam, and his prescription was, to put it succinctly, join a club, right?
sentences.zh: 但我认为很多人觉得在工作和照顾家庭之间，他们没有时间做这件事。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of people feel like they don't have time for that in between work and caretaking.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得他们再也没有时间进行那种劳动密集型的社会联系了。

sentences.en: They don't feel like they've got time anymore for those kinds of labor-intensive social connections.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这也是社会科学家们非常了解的事情。

sentences.en: And this is something that social scientists are also really clued into.
sentences.zh: 我认为现代社会科学中最酷的研究之一是关于“时间富足”（time affluence）这个概念的。

sentences.en: I think one of the coolest bits of work coming out of modern-day social science is on this concept of what's called time affluence.
sentences.zh: 这是哈佛商学院的阿什利·威兰斯（Ashley Willans）的一项出色研究。

sentences.en: This is a lovely work by Ashley Willans at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 时间富足是指在时间上感到富有。

sentences.en: Time affluence is feeling wealthy in time.
sentences.zh: 它不是指你客观上有多少时间，而是指你主观上觉得你有空闲时间留给自己。

sentences.en: It's not how much objective time you have, but it's the subjective sense that you just have free time for yourself.
sentences.zh: 这与现在许多听众——我猜——正在经历的情况恰恰相反，那就是所谓的“时间饥荒”（time famine），你简直是在为时间而挨饿。

sentences.en: It's the opposite of what so many people listening right now, I am guessing, are experiencing, which is what's called time famine, where you're literally starving for time.
sentences.zh: 我认为“饥荒”这个词在生理上是成立的，因为当我们觉得时间不够用时，几乎就像饥荒一样。

sentences.en: And this term famine, I think, works physiologically because when we feel like we don't have enough time, it's almost like famine.
sentences.zh: 它会增加炎症。

sentences.en: It increases inflammation.
sentences.zh: 它会对我们的身体造成所有这些坏处。

sentences.en: It, like, does all these bad things to our body.
sentences.zh: 但有很多研究表明，它对我们的社会联系也有坏处。

sentences.en: But there's lots of work showing that it does bad things to our social connection.
sentences.zh: 你只需要引导人们去思考时间。

sentences.en: You just prime people to think about time.
sentences.zh: 心理学家会用这种俗套的方式来做实验，比如让你重组单词，所有的单词都与时间有关。

sentences.en: Psychologists do these in these cheesy ways where you unscramble words and all the words are about time.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在隐性地思考时间。

sentences.en: So you're kind of implicitly thinking about time.

sentences.zh: 这是一种“既要又要”的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, all these individual things that I'm suggesting are supposed to complement, not substitute the stuff that we should really be doing.
sentences.zh: 我建议的所有这些个人行为，都是为了补充，而不是替代我们真正应该做的那些事。

sentences.en: But another thing we know about individual action is that it just makes us more productive.
sentences.zh: 但关于个人行动，我们知道的另一件事是，它确实让我们更有生产力。

sentences.en: It gives us emotional bandwidth, and that can mean the resilience we need to fight for stuff.
sentences.zh: 它给了我们情感带宽，这可能意味着我们需要为争取权益而奋斗的韧性。

sentences.en: I think people mistakenly think that these individual strategies sometimes build up the resilience you need to just, like, put up with being in a bad society.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们有时会错误地认为，这些个人策略建立的韧性只是为了让你忍受糟糕的社会。

sentences.en: But I think the real goal of them is to give you the resilience to, like, fight the bad society.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它们真正的目标是给你韧性去对抗那个糟糕的社会。

sentences.en: And there's data on this.
sentences.zh: 而且有数据支持这一点。

sentences.en: Konstantin Khrushchev, who's at Georgetown, has this lovely paper that he talks about, the Pollyanna hypothesis, which is this idea, like, it would just make people happy.
sentences.zh: 乔治城大学的康斯坦丁·克鲁什切夫（Konstantin Khrushchev）有一篇很棒的论文，他谈到了“波利安娜假设”，即这种观点：这只会让人快乐。

sentences.en: They're going to be, like, this Delulu Pollyanna walking around, like, everything's great.
sentences.zh: 他们会像个天真的波利安娜一样走来走去，觉得一切都很棒。

sentences.en: Like, all these structures of inequality.
sentences.zh: 就像所有这些不平等的结构一样。

sentences.en: Like, I'm cool with that because, like, fine, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，我对此没意见，因为，好吧，对吧？

sentences.en: And his point in running the paper is, like, well, that's a hypothesis about how human nature works.
sentences.zh: 他写这篇论文的观点是，好吧，这是一个关于人性如何运作的假设。

sentences.en: The hypothesis is, like, if you make people happy, they're just going to ignore the structural stuff.
sentences.zh: 这个假设是，如果你让人快乐，他们就会忽视结构性问题。

sentences.en: And what he finds is just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但他发现的恰恰相反。

sentences.en: If you look at people who are taking action to fix structural problems, he does this in the domain of like climate concern.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看那些正在采取行动解决结构性问题的人，他在气候问题的领域做了研究。

sentences.en: And also he's running this around the times of Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 而且他还在“黑人的命也是命”（Black Lives Matter）运动期间进行了这项研究。

sentences.en: And so who goes to a protest and so on.
sentences.zh: 比如谁会去参加抗议等等。

sentences.en: He finds that like it's the people who have the highest positive emotion, the people with the best mental health that are ones that are going and trying to fix stuff.
sentences.zh: 他发现，正是那些拥有最高积极情绪、心理健康状况最好的人，才是那些去尝试解决问题的人。

sentences.en: It goes back to where we started our conversation around the eudaimonic sense of like, how do you become happy and how do you find meaning?
sentences.zh: 这回到了我们对话开始时关于“幸福感”（eudaimonic）的讨论，即你如何变得快乐以及如何找到意义？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And getting back to the American experiment, right?
sentences.zh: 回到美国实验，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, this was what the forefathers meant, right?
sentences.zh: 这正是先贤们的意思，对吧？

sentences.en: They had problems, right?
sentences.zh: 他们也有问题，对吧？

sentences.en: The forefathers were filled with people who are not focused on everybody's eudaimonic happiness.
sentences.zh: 先贤们中充满了并不关注每个人幸福感的人。

sentences.en: Those unalienable rights are for landed white dudes, not for everybody.
sentences.zh: 那些不可剥夺的权利是给有土地的白人男性的，而不是给所有人的。

sentences.en: But in their idealistic sense, what they were trying to go for is that eudaimonic sense of happiness.
sentences.zh: 但在他们理想主义的意义上，他们所追求的是那种幸福感。

sentences.en: It was about civic virtue.
sentences.zh: 那是关于公民美德。

sentences.en: It was about making everybody happy.
sentences.zh: 那是关于让每个人都快乐。

sentences.en: And that was the happiness they thought we should all be pursuing.
sentences.zh: 而那正是他们认为我们都应该追求的幸福。

sentences.en: Laurie Santos, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 劳里·桑托斯（Laurie Santos），非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I've really enjoyed our conversation.
sentences.zh: 我很享受我们的谈话。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我参加节目。
